summary: Brass: Lancashire is a tight, tense economic puzzle where you build overlapping networks of canals and railways while timing industry sales and loans to maximize two separate scoring rounds. Every turn is an agonizing choice between building your own engine and blocking or piggybacking on opponents' links, with a merciless economy that punishes inefficiency.
praised: Deep, interlocking economic engine with real long-term planning
Clever double-scoring structure (canal era then rail era) rewards timing and flipping tiles at the right moment
High player interaction through shared network links and resource markets
Strong replayability due to variable player counts and card draws
Elegant mechanical unity — every action ties back to the network and resource flow
criticised: Steep learning curve and rules overhead for new players
Downtime and analysis paralysis, especially at higher player counts
Thin theme that's really just a numbers/logistics puzzle
Punishing for beginners playing against experienced players
Some fiddliness tracking coal/iron resource flow along links

interaction.kind: network/route building with blocking, resource competition, and market manipulation

scoring.why: Victory points come from flipped industry tiles plus connected canal/rail links, scored twice across two eras, so efficient network building and well-timed industry development decide the winner.
